title: From Requirements to Manufacturing Readiness
summary: Translating product and process requirements into integrated manufacturing equipment through systematic engineering development, verification and technical coordination.

sections.overview:
My experience in manufacturing automation spans the development and industrialization of automated assembly equipment, connecting product requirements, mechanical systems, automation technology and manufacturing processes.

My responsibilities involve translating engineering requirements into practical equipment solutions, coordinating technical development with equipment suppliers and supporting the transition from concept development to manufacturing readiness.
sections.challenge:
Developing automated manufacturing equipment requires more than designing a machine capable of performing individual operations.

The integrated system must satisfy multiple requirements simultaneously, including process repeatability, product quality, equipment reliability, manufacturability, operational efficiency, maintainability and verification readiness.

The engineering challenge is to manage the interdependencies between product design, manufacturing processes and equipment architecture while addressing technical uncertainties throughout development.
sections.contribution: My individual responsibilities across equipment development and industrialization include:
sections.methodology: Engineering development is iterative rather than strictly linear. Findings from feasibility studies, integration activities and verification may require earlier requirements or design decisions to be reassessed.
sections.decisions: Effective equipment development requires evaluating alternative technical solutions against system-level objectives rather than optimizing individual mechanisms in isolation.
sections.outcomes:
Through my work in equipment development and industrialization, I have contributed to the progression of automated manufacturing systems through technical development, integration, verification and manufacturing-readiness activities.

My approach emphasizes measurable acceptance criteria, systematic technical issue resolution and evidence-based evaluation of equipment and process readiness.
sections.demonstration:
Three planned Engineering Lab tools will directly complement this case study.

These will use independently defined scenarios and synthetic inputs. None will reconstruct actual employer equipment.
sections.reflection:
Manufacturing automation has reinforced my understanding that successful equipment development depends on the interaction between mechanical design, process requirements, automation systems and technical execution.

My engineering approach is to identify critical interfaces early, evaluate alternative solutions systematically and use verification evidence to reduce uncertainty throughout development.

This perspective is applicable across regulated manufacturing, industrial automation, equipment development, new product introduction and complex engineering programs.

contributions: Translating product and process needs into equipment requirements.
Evaluating technical concepts, feasibility and potential design limitations.
Providing manufacturing and assembly input during engineering design reviews.
Coordinating supplier-facing technical discussions and engineering deliverables.
Supporting equipment integration, verification and qualification activities.
Investigating technical issues and identifying opportunities for process improvement.
Coordinating engineering priorities and cross-functional technical alignment.
contributionNote: My contributions form part of multidisciplinary engineering programs involving internal stakeholders and external equipment development partners.

technicalExample.title: Designing a robust component-positioning system
technicalExample.objective: Achieve sufficient positional repeatability for downstream assembly while accommodating expected component dimensional variation.

concepts.title: Rigid positioning
concepts.description: Higher constraint; potentially sensitive to part variation.

concepts.title: Compliant positioning
concepts.description: Tolerance accommodation; requires controlled stiffness and movement.

technicalExample.interpretation:
The important distinction is that a design change intended to improve mechanical repeatability may introduce unfavorable interactions with component tolerances, deformation, gripping forces or downstream operations.

An engineering evaluation should therefore consider the complete process window and verify the selected concept under representative variation.

title: Engineering for Manufacturing Performance
summary: Applying structured engineering analysis, systematic problem-solving and process optimization to improve manufacturing equipment performance and operational reliability.

sections.overview:
My experience in manufacturing process development includes evaluating and improving the performance of automated assembly systems through structured problem-solving, equipment data analysis and systematic engineering investigations.

My approach focuses on understanding the underlying mechanisms contributing to equipment losses rather than addressing isolated symptoms.
sections.challenge:
Manufacturing equipment performance is influenced by interactions between mechanical systems, automation sequences, component variability, process parameters and operating conditions.

The primary engineering challenge is to identify the dominant performance constraints, distinguish recurring technical problems from isolated disturbances and develop corrective actions that improve performance without compromising product quality or process stability.
sections.contribution: My responsibilities in manufacturing performance optimization include:
sections.methodology: The methodology is iterative. New evidence may invalidate an initial hypothesis and require the investigation to return to an earlier stage.
sections.decisions: Manufacturing performance optimization requires balancing equipment productivity with process robustness, product quality and long-term reliability.
sections.outcomes:
Through my process development and optimization responsibilities, I have contributed to technical issue resolution, equipment performance evaluation and manufacturing process stabilization.

My approach emphasizes measurable performance indicators, systematic investigation of recurring losses and verification of corrective action effectiveness under representative operating conditions.
sections.demonstration: Each planned tool will use independently defined engineering assumptions and synthetic data.
sections.reflection:
My experience in manufacturing performance optimization has reinforced the importance of distinguishing symptoms from underlying technical causes.

Effective process improvement requires understanding how mechanical systems, automation sequences, product variability and operating conditions interact. Sustainable improvements depend on valid measurements, sound engineering hypotheses, controlled verification and continued evaluation of process behavior.

These principles are transferable across manufacturing industries, equipment development, new product introduction and operational excellence programs.

contributions: Evaluating equipment performance through operational data and engineering observations.
Investigating recurring assembly, material handling and component-feeding issues.
Analyzing equipment interruptions, rejected components and process variability.
Conducting structured root cause investigations and engineering trials.
Coordinating technical corrective actions with equipment development partners.
Evaluating the effectiveness of implemented improvements.
Supporting process stabilization and manufacturing readiness.
contributionNote: These activities are conducted within multidisciplinary engineering programs, with clearly defined individual and collaborative responsibilities.

title: Leading Complex Engineering Programs
summary: Connecting technical decision-making, multidisciplinary engineering teams and program execution to achieve complex engineering objectives.
role: Senior Process Development Engineer / Functional Team Lead

sections.overview:
My professional experience combines technical engineering responsibilities with the coordination and execution of complex equipment development and industrialization programs.

As a Senior Process Development Engineer with functional engineering team leadership responsibilities, my work extends beyond individual technical deliverables to include engineering prioritization, multidisciplinary coordination, supplier alignment and technical risk management.

My approach is to connect engineering decisions with overall program objectives while maintaining accountability for technical quality and execution readiness.
sections.challenge:
Complex engineering programs involve interconnected technical requirements, multiple stakeholders, external development partners and competing execution priorities.

Individual engineering workstreams may progress independently, but their interfaces and dependencies ultimately determine the readiness of the overall system.

The leadership challenge is to maintain technical alignment, identify emerging risks, resolve dependencies and support timely decisions without compromising engineering integrity.
sections.contribution: My technical leadership and program execution responsibilities include:
sections.methodology: Technical program execution requires continuous feedback between engineering workstreams, risk management and milestone evaluation. Progress should be assessed through technical evidence rather than schedule completion alone.
sections.decisions: These represent general engineering leadership considerations, not disclosures of specific employer decisions.
sections.outcomes:
Through my technical program execution and functional leadership responsibilities, I have contributed to coordinated engineering development, technical issue resolution, supplier alignment and manufacturing readiness activities.

My approach emphasizes clear technical ownership, transparent communication, evidence-based decisions and systematic management of engineering risks and dependencies.
sections.demonstration: These demonstrations will use independently defined scenarios and original engineering models.
sections.reflection:
My experience has reinforced the understanding that effective technical leadership requires both engineering depth and the ability to coordinate complex execution environments.

I believe the role of a technical leader is to create clarity, enable sound engineering decisions, maintain accountability and align individual technical contributions with overall program objectives.

These principles are transferable across manufacturing automation, new product introduction, technical program management and engineering leadership.

contributions: Establishing engineering priorities and coordinating technical workstreams.
Providing functional guidance to a team of three engineers.
Leading supplier-facing technical discussions and engineering alignment.
Coordinating technical deliverables, dependencies and issue resolution.
Supporting cross-functional alignment between engineering, manufacturing, quality and validation stakeholders.

title: Engineering the Mechanics of Advanced Lattice Structures
summary: Investigating the relationship between structural geometry, material distribution and mechanical performance under torsional loading.

references.label: The Effect of Functional Gradient Material Distribution and Patterning on Torsional Properties of Lattice Structures Manufactured Using MultiJet Fusion Technology — Materials (2021), first author

Investigation of torsional properties of surface- and strut-based lattice structures manufactured using MultiJet Fusion technology — The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology (2022), first author

sections.overview:
My graduate research investigated how lattice architecture influences mechanical response under torsion, combining computational geometry, additive manufacturing and experimental characterization.

The work resulted in two first-author journal publications examining surface-based and strut-based lattices, including functionally graded configurations.
sections.challenge:
Designing lightweight structures requires balancing material usage against mechanical performance. Conventional material selection alone cannot fully address the design opportunities introduced by complex cellular geometries.

The central engineering question was how geometric topology, density distribution and unit-cell arrangement influence stiffness, energy absorption and structural failure under twisting loads.
sections.contribution:
As first author of both studies, I contributed to the research and its scientific dissemination.

For the 2021 study, my documented contributions included software implementation, experimental investigation, data preparation, collaborative quantitative analysis, visualization and manuscript development.

These activities formed part of a collaborative research program, with distinct contributions from the other authors.
sections.methodology: The research also addressed the challenge of calculating the polar second moment of area for lattice structures with varying cross-sections.
sections.decisions:
The investigation demonstrates why structural optimization must consider multiple performance criteria simultaneously.

A geometry that maximizes rigidity may not provide the best deformation capacity or energy absorption. Material distribution and topology must therefore be evaluated against the intended loading conditions and acceptable failure mechanisms.
sections.outcomes:
Two peer-reviewed publications documented the research outcomes.

Gyroid exhibited the greatest torsional stiffness among the three configurations, whereas primitive lattice geometry demonstrated stronger energy-absorption capability and greater plastic deformation.

The graded-lattice investigation additionally demonstrated that tailored density could improve stiffness, although increased rigidity could be accompanied by less ductile failure. Circular unit-cell arrangements increased permissible angular deformation without a corresponding stiffness advantage.
sections.demonstration:
The proposed EL-010 — Interactive TPMS & Lattice Structure Explorer will extend this case study into an independently developed educational engineering tool.

Geometry selection, unit-cell visualization, relative-density exploration and simplified mechanical interpretation.

Planned for Phase 6. Not yet implemented.
sections.reflection:
This research reinforced my approach to engineering: connect design intent with measurable performance, understand the limitations of analytical models and evaluate technical trade-offs through experimental evidence.

The resulting capabilities extend beyond additive manufacturing into mechanical systems development, engineering verification, structured experimentation and evidence-based technical decision-making.
